summary: Design model of ChecksHub admission with the owner's F1 rule (a waiting release entry whose own pool is full holds one account place): all 12 frozen properties hold at the stated bounds (largest run 13,578,486 states), all 19 matrix runs end as expected, 26 of 26 mutations detected (run 43498744003). F1 corrected: without the hold, one outside job racing for the place a finishing macOS run frees can keep a waiting release macOS job out; with it, two are needed.

modeled: start: refuse while paused, reuse a green digest, hold and supersede
the pump: lane then arrival, place recorded before the dispatch
dispatch answer, run end, cancel landing
leases: lapse, sweep, no late renew
the account hold: a waiting release entry whose own pool is full holds one account place jobs behind it may not take
abstracted: one macOS pool and one hosted pool under the account limit, one heavy pool
one shared key group and one shared digest group
no clock: a lease lapses at any moment
assumptions: A1 one admission step at a time
A2 the place is in the ledger before the dispatch await
A3 outside jobs counted at once (code lags one poll)
A4 a dispatch is answered and a run ends
A5 lane, pool, key, digest fixed at start

findings.title: A release macOS job could be kept out of a freed macOS place by one outside job; decided: a waiting release entry holds one account place
findings.story: Corrected from run 43494679727's report, which said lower-lane jobs alone keep a waiting release macOS job out once macOS frees. They cannot: every macOS job also counts in the account, so the run that ends frees a macOS place and an account place together, and the pump gives it to the release job first. What the first rule allowed: a land job is admitted into the account's last place while the release job waits for macOS; when the macOS run ends, a job the hub does not govern (another repo's on the account, a person's run) takes the freed account place before the hub dispatches, and the release job finds macOS free and the account full. The owner's decision (Main, d6) makes a waiting release entry whose own pool is full hold one account place that jobs behind it may not take, so the land job is never admitted into it and two outside jobs are needed to block the release job. Mutation no-account-hold (the first rule) breaks ReleaseKeepsItsAccountPlace on MC_account.cfg; NeverBlockedByLaterAdmit shows two outside racers still can. Outside jobs are never governed (design 9.1): the hold is one place of slack, not a guarantee.
